newsitem.title: GERMANY: UAL to keep ex-Germany cargo rates stable.
newsitem.headline: UAL to keep ex-Germany cargo rates stable.

text.p: United Airlines said it will keep official ex-Germany air cargo rates stable this autumn but foresees possible January price increases.
Robert Blythe, the airline's cargo sales manager Germany, told Reuters in an interview: "We will definitely not change our rates in October."
But he added: "If the market continues to pick up, I might do an in-between change on January 1, perhaps to selected destinations."
United normally alters its official rates on October 1 and April 1, he pointed out.
Blythe said: "I would like to increase Chicago but it depends on capacity. If market capacity falls, then that would be in line (for a rise)," he said.
Dallas and the West Coast could also be destinations able to take a rates increase, he added.
Ex-Germany air cargo rates have fallen substantially this year but appeared to have bottomed out now, Blythe said.
"The market seems to be coming back with more tonnage but I believe agents could be getting this volume from outside Germany," he said. --Air Cargo Newsroom tel:+44 171 542 7706 fax:+44 171 542 5017
